amendments.because: Three review rounds kept finding edge cases in the automatic merge (squash merges, worktree cleanup, existing merges); the owner's rule is to simplify a repeatedly breaking area, so the commands now only detect and point to the merge
amendments.done_when: When the default branch has commits to a story's plans/<KEY>.md that its story branch lacks, forge next says so in one plain line with the command to merge the default branch into the story branch, and forge task start merges the default branch into the story branch first (refusing with a plain message, changing nothing, when that merge conflicts) before reading the task rows. Command-level tests cover a plan edited on the default branch after approval, the merge in task start, and a conflicting merge.

done_when: When the default branch's plans/<KEY>.md differs from the story branch's copy and the default branch's last commit touching it is newer than the story branch's, forge next says so in one plain line with the command to merge the default branch into the story branch, and forge task start refuses with the same line, changing nothing. Neither command merges anything. Command-level tests cover a plan edited on the default branch after approval (flagged and refused), identical copies (not flagged), and a newer story-branch edit (not flagged).

findings.body: The Done-when requires one plain line containing both the explanation and merge command. This return emits two lines. Task start likewise emits two because src/forge/repo.py:53 inserts a newline before `Next:`. The new test at tests/test_plan_edits_on_the_default_branch.py:56–60 explicitly expects that two-line output instead of checking the required single-line notice. Render and test the same single-line notice in both commands.
findings.title: Not done: Both commands must emit the same single-line notice containing the merge command

findings.body: The standard requires: “Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change.” The retained compatibility test at tests/test_readloop_gates.py:275–283 edits the default-branch plan but still expects next to recommend starting SHOW and task start to succeed. Those assertions contradict the new refusal behavior. The supplied close run confirms failure at line 280 and a nonzero suite exit. Update the obsolete expectations while preserving the test's older-notes compatibility coverage; do not bypass the new gate to satisfy them.
findings.title: Standard: Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change

findings.body: This test changes “What changes for you” without renewing approval. src/forge/approval.py:84–90 therefore returns a waiting digest, and src/forge/nextstep.py:296–298 returns the approval guidance before reaching plan_behind at line 306. Consequently, this assertion passes without exercising next's newer-story exemption. The task-start assertion exercises the helper, but does not establish the required behavior through next. Change a section outside the approval hash, or read and reapprove the revised plan before checking next.
findings.title: Not done: Test that forge next does not flag a newer story-branch edit

findings.body: The folder is interpolated without shell quoting in both command variants. For a checkout under a path containing spaces, `git -C /path/My Project/... merge origin/main` treats `/path/My` as the directory and fails, leaving the user unable to follow the suggested recovery command as printed. Quote the folder wherever it appears in these commands.
findings.title: Quote worktree paths in the suggested merge commands

why: forge next and forge task start read a story's task rows from its story branch, so a plan edit that reached the default branch another way (a fix) is silently ignored: a client saw a task listed as startable although the merged plan made it wait for a new task
